policies.title: Named ordinary passports: statutory no-visa visits
policies.summary: The 2019 Visa Exemption Regulations expressly exempt these named ordinary-nationality passport holders from the visa default for visitor stays not exceeding six months.
conditions: S.R.O. 37 of 2019 establishes the visa default and expressly names this ordinary-passport cohort for visits not exceeding six months.

The current Government guidance confirms a no-visa route but describes some named countries as three-month visitors rather than six-month visitors. Status is supported; the conflicting duration must be checked with Immigration before travel.

The 2025 and 2026 official amending PDFs establish that the 2019 Regulations have been amended, but the publicly accessible PDFs truncate before the inserted text. They are not used to infer any additional ordinary-passport nationality or duration.
The online ED Card is a free Immigration and Customs declaration, not an ETA or visa. Visa-free status does not remove border, health, customs, security or admission requirements.
This policy excludes residence, work, study, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document, and other non-short-visitor routes.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: conditional 21-day tourist exemption
policies.summary: The current Government entry guidance expressly says any bona fide tourist or transit passenger with a return ticket may enter without a visa when the Immigration Officer is satisfied that the stay will not exceed 21 days.
conditions: This is an express, conditional short-visitor route: the traveller must be a bona fide tourist or in transit, possess a return ticket, and satisfy the Immigration Officer that the intended stay does not exceed 21 days.

The status does not establish a stay longer than 21 days, work, study, residence, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, special-document or other purpose. The Immigration Officer retains the stated satisfaction test.

The 2019 statutory default requires a visa unless an exemption applies. The currently accessible Government guidance independently reproduces this all-tourist 21-day exemption; it is not inferred from visa-form availability or nationality-list omission.

The 2025 and 2026 amendment PDFs are published but truncate before the inserted provisions. No claimed status relies on guessing their nationality or document scope; their existence is a material recheck risk.
The online ED Card is a free Immigration and Customs declaration, not an ETA or visa.
